gaps.quote: Every fixed-tape procedure of the argument comes from one and the same network
gaps.note: False. The paper (line 114) says 'Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values'; each procedure has its own network, not one shared network.

gaps.quote: so the paper fixes every intermediate frame to the identity
gaps.note: Wrong and does not follow. The telescoping holds for any intermediate frames, so it cannot force them to be the identity. The paper (lines 155-156, 824-825) says the intermediate frames are chosen to make each edge change inexpensive (implementable by smaller calls to the same procedure), once the endpoint frames are fixed.

gaps.quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator $D_\nu$ on arrays indexed by the common address set
gaps.note: The page never says what sources, sinks, nodes, edges and routes of the network are (the paper: the vertices on a wire are its source, the gates touching it in time order, and its sink; edges join consecutive vertices), nor what the common address set is. The reader has no picture of the graph the frames are attached to.

gaps.quote: By the telescoping, the route applies
gaps.note: Telescoping only shows that a chain of edge operators along one wire collapses. A route from input role w to output role rho(w) passes through gates that combine several wires, so the endpoint-only conclusion needs the gate-commuting identity applied to the whole network and the convention that the supplied physical input has logical interpretation D_source^{-1} applied (paper lines 141-142, 816-822). The page states neither the whole-network operator nor this input convention.
